why:
Measured against the recorded upstream surfaces (`docs/reference/api-surface/{rclc,rclcpp,rclrs}.json`): none of them contains `park`, `wake_source`, `spin_nominal` or `granularity` at all, so there is no upstream name to align to. Same basis as the `Executor::release_jitter` pair beside it.

phase-436, re-exported by B2 — `Executor::last_park` RETURNS one and `register_wake_source` hands one back, so without a path a caller outside the crate could receive a value it cannot name or match on. `CallerBudget` / `Timer` / `Session` / `Platform(u8)`: which deadline source won the last park. Attribution costs one byte per spin and is the difference between a schedulability argument you can audit and one you have to trust; rclrs reports no wake cause at all. (Shard: `topics.py` routes this key to this file rather than to exec/, where its `Executor::register_wake_source` / `Executor::last_park` siblings live — the same split `c:deadline_policy_t` records. The verdict is right; the shard is an artifact of the key's wording.)
